item.title: Dolly Babe Almost Traded Rap For Nails Before Pink Blush Takes Off
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Dolly Babe says she considered a $700 nail class before recording Pink Blush on her phone and landing her breakout hit.
item.content:encoded:
Dolly Babe nearly traded rap for a nail technician course before a bedroom recording changed her plans. The Dallas rapper discussed her backup career in a V-103 interview with DJ Sturgess published Tuesday on its YouTube channel.

"So I was going to be a nail tech," Dolly said. She had searched Google for legitimate ways to make money and considered paying $700 for a class. The idea came while she was weighing a practical way to earn outside music.

Instead, she recorded "Pink Blush" on her phone while alone in her room. After years of studio sessions, she said she lacked the motivation to book another and released the recording without mixing or mastering.

"That was the fastest a song has ever moved for me," she told Sturgess. Earlier viral moments had failed to last, leaving her ready to stop making music.

The June 30 single became her summer breakout and later received a remix featuring Megan Thee Stallion. A November 9 HITS profile put its Hot 100 debut at No. 58 and reported 3.3 million monthly Spotify listeners. It also counted more than 17 million video views and celebrity engagement from Rihanna, Madonna and Janet Jackson.

Radio followed the online response, with the single impacting Urban stations September 21. HITS reported that it became the most added record at both Urban and Rhythmic radio, counting 42 Urban adds and 51 Rhythmic adds. Her music also appeared on Spotify playlists including New Music Friday, Feelin' Myself, New Joints and Most Necessary, the profile noted.

Her follow-up single "Hittin" arrived October 27 through Princess Pink LLC under an exclusive license to 300 Entertainment, with the streaming listing giving its running time as two minutes. The label has its own history with her remix collaborator: Megan was on its roster when Warner Music Group acquired 300 in December 2021.

Dolly also told Sturgess she was working on her first official project without committing to an imminent release. She wanted that debut to meet her standards before giving listeners a finished collection.

She named Beyoncé as the artist she most wanted to collaborate with.

item.title: Milagro Gramz Challenges Judge’s One-Sentence Ruling In Megan Thee Stallion Appeal
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Milagro Gramz presses her appeal over an unexplained ruling as Megan Thee Stallion's lawyers defend the $75,000 judgment.
item.content:encoded:
Milagro Gramz is putting a judge’s one-sentence rejection at the center of her latest fight with Megan Thee Stallion, arguing that an unexplained ruling leaves an important question about impartiality unanswered.

Her reply brief in the Eleventh Circuit challenges the denial of her request to reopen the judgment. The blogger says the appeals court cannot properly review that decision without knowing how the judge evaluated her conflict allegations.

“Public confidence is not restored by a paperless ‘denied,'” Milagro wrote.

The dispute concerns U.S. District Judge Cecilia Altonaga’s husband, George Mencio Jr., and his position at Holland & Knight. Milagro points to the firm’s representation of Roc Nation CEO Desiree Perez in separate litigation, alongside Megan’s trial testimony about conversations with Perez.

Those connections, Milagro argues, create an appearance problem even without proof of actual bias.

Megan’s lawyers already rejected that reasoning. They also argue that federal procedural rules permit judges to reject this type of motion without issuing a written opinion.

They say neither the judge’s husband nor his firm appeared in this lawsuit, and the connections Milagro describes do not justify undoing the result.

“The judge’s spouse did not appear in this case. His firm did not appear in this case,” Megan’s attorneys wrote.

The two sides also disagree about whether Milagro waited too long. She says supporters alerted her to the spouse-firm relationship on May 29, and she investigated before filing her motion on July 7.

Megan’s team argues that the information was public before trial and that Milagro raised the issue only after losing other attempts at relief. Milagro counters that public availability does not establish when she actually learned the relevant facts.

“A bond motion is not a recusal motion,” Milagro wrote, rejecting the suggestion that her earlier request concerning payment should have included this challenge.

AllHipHop previously covered her appeal following the bond dispute, part of the continuing battle over Megan’s $75,000 judgment.

Her challenge to the underlying judgment and this separate appeal have been consolidated for disposition.

item.title: Beastie Boys Take “Licensed To Ill” At 40 To Jon Stewart & SmartLess
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Beastie Boys line up two anniversary interviews as a new vinyl edition revisits the debut that took rap to No. 1.
item.content:encoded:
Beastie Boys are taking the 40th anniversary of Licensed to Ill to The Daily Show with Jon Stewart and the SmartLess podcast, with Ad-Rock and Mike D set for both appearances on November 16.

The conversations accompany a new edition of the album that first took rap to No. 1 on the Billboard 200.

The duo’s appearances are part of the anniversary campaign. Def Jam Recordings and UMe are preparing a two-LP Vinylphyle reissue for March 18, 2027, months after the original album’s November 15 birthday.

The new pressing also deals with a less visible part of keeping a 40-year-old record in circulation: aging master tapes. Sterling Sound engineer Joe Nino-Hernes worked from a high-resolution digital transfer of the original 1986 quarter-inch master rather than repeatedly running the tapes.

“It also allowed me to minimize handling of the tapes that have become fragile with time,” Nino-Hernes explained.

He said his chosen process preserved fidelity better than cutting from a second-generation analog copy. The transfer used the same machine and electronics he employs when cutting records.

Chuck D contributes fresh liner notes to the package, continuing a connection that reaches back well beyond this anniversary. The Public Enemy co-founder also honored the group when Beastie Boys entered the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2012.

Ad-Rock and Mike D attended that Cleveland ceremony without MCA, who was ill. The tribute performance featured The Roots, Travie McCoy and Kid Rock covering music from the group’s catalog.

Before those honors, the trio had opened for Madonna in 1985 and built its early recording career at Def Jam. Rick Rubin and the group produced Licensed to Ill, whose singles included “Brass Monkey,” “Paul Revere” and “No Sleep Till Brooklyn.”

The album received its RIAA Diamond certification in 2015. Later Beastie Boys albums Ill Communication and Hello Nasty also reached No. 1, extending their chart history beyond the debut.

The anniversary edition preserves its 13-song sequence across three sides, leaving the fourth for a band-logo etching rather than additional audio.

The package includes a four-panel insert reproducing scans of the original tape boxes.

item.title: Snow Tha Product Refuses To Stay Quiet For The Music Business
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Snow Tha Product weighs the career cost of speaking up as she balances community advocacy with running her own operation.
item.content:encoded:
Snow Tha Product isn’t letting the music business decide which communities she’s allowed to defend. She’s speaking up for women, Latino communities and queer people even when that choice can complicate her career.

In a November 9 interview with Remezcla, she connected that stance to everyday needs rather than industry approval. “I wish, you know, having clean water didn’t become political,” Snow Tha Product said.

The conversation also covered the doubts imposed on her as a first-generation Latina and what younger women might hear in her music. Snow wants them to trust themselves instead of absorbing other people’s limits.

Her new project, Next Time, Believe Me, opens with “Should’ve Been Worse,” a title that feeds directly into her thoughts about staying quiet. “They benefit from our silence. Just remember that,” Snow Tha Product told Remezcla.

She’s discussing those choices while running a business with family members on her team. Independence hasn’t removed the larger companies from the picture, and she said she still has to operate around their power.

That business question has followed her through more than one career chapter. Snow’s Atlantic Records signing in 2012 put her inside a major label after she built attention through her own releases.

“I just wanna be able to one day live happily ever after in my home and not feel like people are gonna come to attack us,” Snow tha Product said.

Back then, she was already making a point of protecting the brands she’d created before the deal. She kept its terms private while discussing a balance between her established identity and the opportunities a larger company could offer.

The latest release carries Snow Tha Product, Inc. on its recording copyright line, with Universal Music Latino handling distribution. Across 17 songs and roughly 40 minutes, the project brings several collaborators into that setup. Solo songs include “QUE TE DUELA,” “BESTIE” and “Come For Me,” with the sequence moving between English and Spanish titles across its November 6 full digital release.

Zhavia joins “Blame It On Me,” while Toni Romiti appears on “Was It Something?” Gera MX, Chuzzington and AJ Hernz also appear, giving the middle of the tracklist a run of collaborations between Snow’s solo records.

Tech N9ne appears on the closing title track, which runs two minutes and three seconds.

item.title: Teyana Taylor Defends Cheering Amy Madigan After Oscars Loss
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Teyana Taylor stands by her Oscars applause for Amy Madigan, explaining the friendship behind her much-discussed reaction.
item.content:encoded:
Teyana Taylor is defending her applause for Amy Madigan after losing their Oscars category. She says their friendship made her enthusiasm genuine.

“Whether I win or lose, I’m going to celebrate my peers,” Taylor told Allure in its November 12 cover interview. The two supported each other throughout awards season.

Madigan won Best Supporting Actress for Weapons at the March 15 ceremony. Taylor was nominated for One Battle After Another, alongside Wunmi Mosaku for Sinners and Sentimental Value performers Elle Fanning and Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas.

Taylor’s film still had a major night. One Battle After Another won Best Picture, while Paul Thomas Anderson took Best Director and Sean Penn won Best Supporting Actor.

The Oscars also brought a separate, tense moment for Taylor after the ceremony. AllHipHop covered her confrontation with a security guard as she tried to rejoin her cast for a Best Picture photograph.

Earlier in the season, Taylor had received an ovation herself. Her performance earned her the supporting-actress Golden Globe in January, and in her acceptance speech, she addressed Black women and girls watching.

Taylor won that Golden Globe on January 11.

item.title: Dave Returns To TV In Cristiano Ronaldo’s Day 1s First Look
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Dave steps into Cristiano Ronaldo's football drama as new production photos put him on the couch with Damian Lewis.
item.content:encoded:
Dave is taking his acting career into football’s business world, sitting opposite Damian Lewis in Day 1s. Cristiano Ronaldo’s new production update gives the British rapper a place in the first images from the television project.

An Instagram carousel includes a still of Dave and Lewis sitting on a couch beneath a framed Ronaldo jersey. It’s a different setting from Top Boy, the Netflix crime drama that brought Dave’s acting to a wider audience.

Ronaldo confirmed the production news in his own post, writing: “Exciting news! Production of my first TV show, Day 1s, has just started. More to come!” His announcement doesn’t name Dave’s character or explain how much of the series he’ll appear in.

The series centers on Stanley Dalton, a football agent played by Lewis.

Ronaldo and filmmaker Matthew Vaughn are behind the project through their UR Marv studio, putting a real football star on the production side of a fictional football story.

Dave previously played Modie in Netflix’s 2019 revival of Top Boy alongside returning stars Ashley Walters and Kano. His audition landed him a role initially intended for an older actor, rather than his music career securing the job.

The show’s comeback also placed Dave alongside fellow musician Little Simz and newcomer Micheal Ward in a cast assembled for 10 episodes.

Drake served among the executive producers when Netflix revived the drama after its original run ended in 2013.

For Dave, the new role still adds another television credit beyond the recording booth.

His earlier work on Top Boy also connected his acting and music, with two tracks, “Professor X” and “God’s Eye,” included on the show’s 2019 soundtrack.

That collection brought together performers from the series and other British artists, including Little Simz, Headie One and AJ Tracey. Dave’s next screen appearance takes him into a different kind of British drama, with Lewis playing a man whose business revolves around professional players.

Ronaldo’s latest post leaves the viewing details open, without naming a broadcaster or giving a premiere date.

The image shows Dave on set rather than a trailer revealing his dialogue or storyline. Ronaldo and Vaughn announced their independent studio partnership in April 2025.

item.title: Motown Museum Brings Hitsville Tours Back Before Its 2027 Expansion
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Motown Museum sets a December return for the historic Detroit house as restoration gives way to a new visitor experience.
item.content:encoded:
Motown Museum is reopening the little Detroit house that helped change American music before its much larger expansion opens.

Public tours of Hitsville U.S.A. resume December 17, according to the museum’s reopening announcement.

Visitors have been unable to take the house tour since January while preservation work and construction continued across the property.

That means a return to the building where Berry Gordy established Motown Records in 1959. The address on West Grand Boulevard became a recording home for Marvin Gaye, Stevie Wonder, The Supremes and other artists whose records traveled far beyond Detroit.

The restored tour will also introduce “Hello Detroit,” a permanent gallery on the second floor.

It focuses on the city itself and the conditions that helped Motown’s music take shape, giving visitors more to explore beyond the familiar hit records.

The work has included protecting Studio A’s original character after decades of use. Its floors, walls and sound are part of what the museum is trying to preserve while bringing people back inside.

The house’s December return comes ahead of the broader Motown Experience planned for 2027. That $75 million expansion includes a theater, interactive exhibits and additional ways to explore the label’s archives, with the original Hitsville building remaining part of the campus.

The museum has been preserving that history since Esther Gordy Edwards founded it in 1985. Its collection includes costumes, photographs and company artifacts, along with the upstairs living space Gordy and his family used during the label’s early years.

Its visitors have included artists from later generations, too. Ms. Lauryn Hill took a private tour with her family in 2023, a visit the museum celebrated publicly.

Adult admission for the returning tours is $25, with several discounted categories listed at $21.50. Tours last about an hour, and tickets are tied to a specific date and time rather than open-ended admission.

The final guided tour of each operating day starts at 5 P.M.

item.title: Travis Thompson Trades Rap's Approval Chase For Sobriety & Screenwriting
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Travis Thompson puts movie and TV writing on his agenda while opening up about recovery and a life beyond rap validation.
item.content:encoded:
Travis Thompson wants a writing career beyond the recording booth as sobriety changes what he expects from his music and himself. In a new interview with Seattle Refined, the Burien rapper described plans to make films and television alongside friends without abandoning music.

"I'll rap and tour until I can't, but I really want to make movies and TV with my friends," Travis Thompson said. Acting remains part of that plan, although writing holds the stronger pull.

His reset followed a rough period after leaving Epic Records in 2022. Thompson said a difficult night after a European tour in 2023 led him to call his manager, who suggested Alcoholics Anonymous. Thompson said sobriety has left him calmer and less concerned with proving his rap skills while making songs that connect with people.

That interest in storytelling already has a screen connection through Turtle Island Rap, a documentary directed by Alexandra Lazarowich. Alongside Thompson, the film follows Wiidaaseh and A$h Da Hunter through performances, their personal lives and the work behind their music.

The 97-minute project comes from Scenario Media and Ultimate Cree, with Bell Media listed as its broadcaster. Its focus puts Indigenous artists and their communities at the center of the film rather than using them as background.

Thompson had already appeared on Reservation Dogs before the documentary, discussing Indigenous representation in a 2023 interview. His move into acting gives the screenwriting ambition a connection to work he has already done outside music.

The filmmaker behind his documentary brings experience on both sides of that divide. Lazarowich wrote for the third and fourth seasons of Resident Alien while building a career in documentary production.

His early path also ran through The Residency, the Seattle youth program that helped connect him with Macklemore. The program provides professional studio access and mentoring at no cost to participants, with practical support such as meals, transportation and stipends. Macklemore has publicly discussed his own experience with addiction and sobriety.

Turtle Island Rap is scheduled for its Alberta premiere at Calgary's Globe Cinema on November 21 at 4:30 p.m. during the city's CUFF.Docs Documentary Film Festival.

item.title: NVIDIA’s Suno Investor Fights Music Labels Over Court Testimony
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: NVIDIA's investment arm resists a Suno deposition as Universal and Sony seek answers about the AI company's business.
item.content:encoded:
NVIDIA’s venture arm wants out of a courtroom showdown over what it knew before investing in Suno. NVentures has asked a federal judge to block Universal Music Group and Sony’s demand for sworn testimony in their copyright case against the AI music company.

Eminem‘s publisher, Eight Mile Style, has separately demanded roughly $41 million from Suno over alleged copying. That complaint covers 269 compositions, including “Lose Yourself” and “Stan,” and does not name the rapper as a plaintiff.

In its November 10 California court motion, NVentures says it already supplied 6,324 documents totaling 28,194 pages. The firm argues that the labels should question Suno about its training data and operations instead of requiring an investor to explain them.

“It holds no board, observer, or advisory position with Suno,” NVentures’ lawyers wrote in the motion.

The companies are still contesting 10 subjects for questioning after negotiations narrowed the original subpoena. Those include investment research, licensing costs and communications about the legal risks attached to Suno’s training data.

NVentures participated in Suno’s November 2025 funding round, after the labels had already sued. It asks the judge to cancel the subpoena or restrict its scope.

That financing brought Suno $250 million at a $2.45 billion valuation, with Menlo leading the round and Hallwood Media, Lightspeed and Matrix also participating. The company subsequently raised more than $400 million in June 2026.

Universal and Sony began their underlying lawsuit in June 2024, accusing Suno of training its technology on recordings without permission. Warner Music Group initially joined them but settled in November 2025 and entered a licensing agreement.

The investor fight also reaches beyond NVIDIA. Lightspeed Venture Partners, which holds a Suno board seat, has challenged a separate subpoena, while a judge allowed the labels to question former Menlo Ventures principal C.C. Gong about a deleted social-media post.

Universal has another relationship with NVIDIA outside the litigation. The companies announced an AI collaboration in January involving the chipmaker’s Music Flamingo model, with safeguards for artists and copyright among its stated aims.

The labels’ responses to the two motions filed by NVentures and parent company NVIDIA are due November 24.

item.title: Queen Latifah & The Roots Join 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Queen Latifah adds a Thanksgiving TV date as The Roots, Keke Palmer and Wyclef Jean join Macy's milestone celebration.
item.content:encoded:
Queen Latifah is heading into Thanksgiving with another national television appearance, joining the performers announced for the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. The November 26 event will also feature The Roots with Jimmy Fallon, Keke Palmer and Wyclef Jean.

The lineup arrived Friday, ahead of a milestone broadcast that brings several generations of entertainers to New York. Viewers can watch on NBC, Peacock and Telemundo beginning at 8:30 A.M. ET.

“We’re creating a celebration of unprecedented scale and will deliver an unforgettable Thanksgiving for millions across the country,” Macy’s chief marketing officer Sharon Otterman said.

The parade will follow another major career honor for Latifah: her November 14 induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Her television schedule has expanded, too, after she joined The Voice as a coach for its 30th season alongside Kelly Clarkson, Adam Levine and Riley Green.

That range stretches back decades, from the demo that brought her a Tommy Boy deal in 1988 to her work on Living Single and in Set It Off. The Rock Hall recognition follows a BET Lifetime Achievement Award in 2021 and the addition of her debut album to the National Recording Registry in 2023, a first for a female rapper.

“Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade brings the extraordinary together: iconic entertainers and emerging talent, artistry and imagination, hometown pride, cherished traditions and the thrill of discovering something new,” Otterman added.

The holiday lineup also includes JoJo, Natalie Merchant, DEVO, Anthony Ramos, Leslie Odom Jr. and the Indigo Girls. Teddy Swims and Megan Moroney are scheduled to perform in front of Macy’s 34th Street flagship, while other performers will travel along the route on floats.

Macy’s first staged the parade in 1924, but the event was interrupted for three years during World War II. The centennial edition will feature 100 inflatable elements along the route.

EJAE and RIIZE bring K-pop representation to the broadcast, with Feid and Icona Pop also included in the announced roster. Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb and Al Roker will host, and organizers have more performers and Broadway participants left to announce.

Megan Hilty will lead a tribute to Dolly Parton during the parade.
